q: Sometimes a physical quantity is too big (or) too small to be conveniently expressed in ____.
e: Sometimes a physical quantity is too big (or) too small to be conveniently expressed in basic SI units. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.
Prefixes are multiples or sub-multiples of 10. The physics in this sentence is built around Prefixes.

q: Scientific notation (or) standard form may be written as follows: Place the decimal point after the first ____.
e: Scientific notation (or) standard form may be written as follows: Place the decimal point after the first nonzero digit. The physics in this sentence is built around nonzero digit.

q: Then determine the ____ by counting the number of places we have moved the original decimal point to the marked decimal point.
e: Then determine the power of 10 by counting the number of places we have moved the original decimal point to the marked decimal point. The physics in this sentence is built around power of 10.

q: If we moved the point to the left, then power is ____ and if we moved it to the right, it is negative.
e: If we moved the point to the left, then power is positive and if we moved it to the right, it is negative. The physics in this sentence is built around positive.
